skills.trigger: When evaluating a completely opaque hemithorax to distinguish pulmonary aplasia from total lung collapse (atelectasis) or severe destructive lung disease.
steps: Inspect the expected location of the pulmonary hilum on the affected side for the presence or absence of vascular shadows.

Differentiate based on hilar structures: In pulmonary aplasia, the pulmonary artery and hilar vessels are congenitally absent, resulting in a complete lack of hilar density. In contrast, total atelectasis or severe bronchiectasis with collapse will typically retain visible (though displaced or distorted) pulmonary vascular markings and a definable hilum.
